sources.title: MD3471 City Hall Developer Investment Fund
sources.verified_claim: The Mayor approved receipt of up to £324.39 million to establish CHDIF, initially focused on unlocking stalled sites able to deliver completions by summer 2029 or earlier.

sources.title: City Hall Developer Investment Fund
sources.verified_claim: CHDIF is a £324 million London-wide fund intended to unlock stalled developments, accelerate supply and increase social and affordable homes, with a shared goal of committing funding for at least 5,000 homes by March 2029.

sources.title: City Hall Developer Investment Fund funding guidance
sources.verified_claim: CHDIF guidance states EOIs remain open until funding is committed or closure is confirmed; projects are assessed for strategic fit, delivery, affordability and public-sector intervention, and funding may use loans, recoverable funding or grants.

sources.title: City Hall Developer Investment Fund bidding guidance
sources.verified_claim: The official bidding guide defines the OPS application route and requires organisations to submit formal expressions of interest; programme existence alone does not imply any sample parcel has received funding.

sources.title: Housing and Land funding programmes
sources.verified_claim: City Hall's live portfolio lists CHDIF as open with £324 million and the 2026-36 Social and Affordable Homes Programme with up to £11.7 billion, providing funding-capacity context rather than parcel-specific awards.

sources.title: Small Sites for Small Builders site release fund
sources.verified_claim: The Small Sites programme offers up to £250,000 for investigations, due diligence and feasibility on public or registered-provider land intended for housing delivery, and reports 72 sites released through prior support.

sources.title: Small Sites for Small Builders: site release fund funding guidance
sources.verified_claim: The funding guidance specifies due-diligence and feasibility support, an award range up to £250,000 and a 10 July 2026 application deadline; it is predevelopment support, not a development consent or parcel award.

sources.title: Mayor's Homes for Londoners Land Fund delivers £50 million investment
sources.verified_claim: City Hall announced £50 million from repaid Land Fund resources to support more than 500 affordable homes across London by March 2032, demonstrating an active capital-delivery channel without identifying the three sample parcels.
